example.detection_method: Deploy AI-driven deepfake audio detection integrated with VoIP monitoring systems to analyze call streams for synthetic voice anomalies; correlate with email security gateway logs identifying unusual email requests containing urgent wire transfers; enforce multi-factor and multi-channel employee verification for high-value financial transactions; monitor for anomalous PowerShell activity triggered from email clients; track and alert on new domain registrations mimicking vendor names combined with suspicious URL visits.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1609 - Container and Resource Discovery (VoIP and call metadata analysis)
T1598 - Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment (email with malicious attachment or link)
T1552 - Unsecured Credentials (use of spoofed or compromised email account)
T1204 - User Execution (user opening email and executing payload)
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (HTTP(s) traffic with suspicious URLs)
T1133 - External Remote Services (VoIP call abuse)

validation.comments: The sample accurately represents the problem of AI-enabled deepfake social engineering attacks. It describes a realistic scenario where an attacker uses AI-generated deepfake audio to impersonate the CEO and trick the finance department into wiring funds to a fraudulent account, which aligns perfectly with the problem nature. The technical data is comprehensive and includes relevant email headers, email body, SMTP logs, VoIP call metadata with RTP stream analysis indicating synthetic voice anomalies, wire transfer logs, deepfake detection tool output, employee training logs, multi-channel verification attempts, domain registration details, suspicious URLs, network packet captures, and process creation chains showing suspicious PowerShell commands. The indicators clearly explain why the sample matches the problem, highlighting the unusual wire transfer, suspicious email URL, synthetic voice detection, failed verification, new suspicious domain, and malicious PowerShell activity. The detection method is well detailed and aligns with the recommended risk reduction strategies. Relevant MITRE techniques are appropriately selected and cover the attack vectors involved. Overall, the sample is complete, realistic, and technically accurate, providing a strong example of the stated cybersecurity problem.
